observations.text: SP completed the intercept to the arc and the maintenance of the arc only with the IP directing the lead point computation and part of the turn to the arc. Distance from the arc reached 2.6 DME before a correction toward the arc was established. Performance was at the desired code for this Training Section but marginal; independent lead point computation and earlier recognition of arc closure are expected to improve.

SP, applying the briefed lead point rule, initiated the turn to the arc and maintained the arc after the IP's verbal prompts on the bearing pointer, recognizing the displacement with slight delay. Distance from the arc peaked at 2.0 DME and the aircraft was then flown back onto the arc by the SP, without IP intervention on the controls. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a maintained cross-check between DME and bearing pointer, intercepted the arc close to the computed lead point and made only small errors in the arc maintenance corrections. Distance from the arc did not exceed 1.5 DME and each deviation was recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP computed the lead point for the groundspeed flown, rolled onto the arc with the correct bank and maintained the arc with timely, small heading corrections. Distance from the arc remained within 0.7 DME on both intercepts, executed with accuracy and speed. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP performed intercepts both to and from the arc with precise lead point computation and rolled out on the arc with immediate, minimal control inputs. Deviations were negligible, with distance from the arc within 0.2 DME throughout and an uninterrupted instrument cross-check. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect lead point computation for the groundspeed flown, did not initiate the turn to the arc at the required distance and did not establish the arc after the roll-out. The result was a distance from the arc of 3.0 DME, with the IP directing the turn and flying part of the re-intercept back onto the arc. Further study of the arc intercept technique is required.

SP, due to poor workload distribution, with navigation, communication and aircraft control attempted simultaneously, did not monitor the DME during the intercept and did not arrest the closure toward the arc. The result was a distance from the arc of 2.9 DME inside the arc, corrected only after the IP took the aircraft and re-established the arc.

SP performed the intercept to the arc and maintained the arc within the standard required for this Training Section. Errors in the rate of turn onto the arc were recognized and corrected with delay, after the IP's verbal prompts, with the distance from the arc reaching 2.0 DME. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier recognition of arc closure from the bearing pointer is expected to improve.

SP, due to a consistent cross-check of DME against the bearing pointer, initiated the turn to the arc close to the computed lead point and made only minor errors in the arc maintenance corrections. Distance from the arc did not exceed 1.6 DME and each deviation was recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP computed the lead point correctly for the groundspeed flown and rolled onto the arc with the appropriate bank, then maintained the arc with timely heading corrections. Distance from the arc remained within 0.8 DME on both intercepts, with accuracy and speed in the corrections applied. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP performed intercepts to and from the arc with precise lead point computation and immediate, minimal control corrections, keeping the instrument cross-check uninterrupted. Deviations were negligible, with distance from the arc within 0.3 DME throughout. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to use of a fixed lead distance that did not account for the groundspeed and bank flown, did not begin the turn to the arc in time and overshot the arc without applying a correction toward it. The result was a distance from the arc of 3.2 DME outside the arc, with the IP directing the intercept heading and completing part of the correction. Review of the arc lead point computation is required.

SP, due to attention captured by a minor system indication while the aircraft state went unmonitored, did not maintain the DME cross-check while established on the arc and did not correct the developing drift off the arc. The result was a distance from the arc of 2.7 DME, regained only after the IP directed the turn back onto the arc.

SP, due to correcting toward the arc with heading changes too small for the displacement, did not re-establish the arc after the initial roll-out and allowed the deviation to persist. Distance from the arc reached 2.0 DME and the arc was regained only after the IP's verbal prompts, with the error recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to task sequencing that concentrated all cockpit workload inside the turn, did not monitor the closure rate toward the arc and did not lead the roll-out onto the arc distance. Distance from the arc reached 2.0 DME inside the arc; recognition and correction followed the IP's verbal prompts and were completed with delay.

SP performed the intercepts to and from the arc and maintained the arc within the desired standards. Corrections applied on the arc were slightly late on two occasions, with the distance from the arc reaching 1.5 DME, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - shorter DME cross-check intervals while on the arc are expected to improve.

SP computed the lead point correctly for the groundspeed and rolled onto the arc with the appropriate bank, maintaining the arc with small, timely heading corrections. Distance from the arc remained within 0.6 DME on both intercepts, demonstrating accuracy and speed without IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP intercepted the arc from both an inbound and an outbound course with precise lead point computation and rolled out on the arc with immediate, minimal corrections. Distance from the arc remained within 0.2 DME throughout, with negligible deviations and an uninterrupted instrument cross-check. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to selecting a bank for the turn to the arc that did not match the computed lead point, did not roll out on the arc distance and did not apply a correction toward the arc. The result was a distance from the arc of 3.4 DME, with the IP directing and flying part of the re-intercept. Further practice in arc intercept and arc maintenance is required.

SP, due to over-reliance on automation that was not fully understood, accepted the navigation display presentation without an independent DME check and did not maintain the arc. The result was a distance from the arc of 2.8 DME, with the IP directing the correction back onto the arc.

SP, due to a delayed roll-out from the turn to the arc, did not stabilize the aircraft on the arc distance and applied corrections insufficient to close the displacement. Distance from the arc reached 2.0 DME and the arc was regained only after the IP's verbal prompts, with the error recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to an interrupted instrument cross-check while attention remained on the course indications, did not monitor the DME during the intercept and did not detect the developing displacement from the arc. Distance from the arc reached 2.0 DME; recognition and correction were achieved only after the IP's verbal prompts and were completed with delay.

SP, due to heading corrections on the arc slightly larger than the displacement required, did not hold the arc distance steady and produced repeated small excursions to either side of the arc. Distance from the arc reached 1.4 DME, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention.

SP, due to distraction by a secondary cockpit task during the intercept, did not begin the turn to the arc exactly at the computed lead point and rolled out slightly inside the arc. Distance from the arc reached 1.6 DME, with the deviation recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention.

SP performed the intercepts to and from the arc and maintained the arc with accuracy and speed, within the desired standards. Distance from the arc remained within 0.9 DME, close to the limit of the standard, and one roll-out required a prompt second correction toward the arc. Marginal performance for the Training Section - refinement of the lead point computation is expected to improve consistency.

SP computed the lead point precisely for the groundspeed flown, rolled onto the arc with immediate and minimal control inputs, and maintained the arc with an uninterrupted DME and bearing pointer cross-check. Deviations were negligible, with distance from the arc within 0.2 DME on both intercepts. Above end of block MIF achieved.
